svg.title: A client is starting total parenteral nutrition through a central line. Which outcome should the nurse include in the plan of care?
svg.desc: The dextrose load in TPN makes glycemic control a central, measurable target that the nurse monitors with point-of-care testing. A 5-pound gain in 2 days is tempting because weight gain is the point of nutritional support, but that much weight that fast reflects fluid retention, not restored lean tissue.

g.text: STUDY HUB / QUESTION MAP
TPN Planning
Read the situation
A client is starting total parenteral
nutrition through a central line. Which
outcome should the nurse include in the
plan of care?
What fits here
The client's blood glucose will remain
between 140 and 180 mg/dL during the
infusion
Why it fits
The dextrose load in TPN makes glycemic
control a central, measurable target that
the nurse monitors with point-of-care
testing. A 5-pound gain in 2 days is
tempting because weight gain is the point
of nutritional support, but that much
weight that fast reflects fluid retention,
not restored lean tissue.
